Following the ward preparation protocol, Dr. Sakaguchi personally administers Anna Takahashi’s enema.
strings.patient_bundles.patient_ann.patient.name: Anna Takahashi
strings.patient_bundles.patient_ann.patient.reac: "I feel someone pressing there. Is this pressure normal?" (The palm of my hand is also too hot...The area being pressed is suddenly clearer than elsewhere, so don't press there.)
"It's still a little tight after pressing it. Has the anesthesia fully taken effect?" (If you press it any more, I will scream...don't make me scream.)
"Wait a minute, don't press it! It hurts too much! Be gentler!" (The whole piece hurts when you press it... Is it necessary to press it to death? The knife is really about to come off.)

"That's it? I'm already lying down. At least let me know what will happen next." (That's it? Just strip down and lie here waiting for the operation, and the result is just one sentence? It's a bit unreal.)
"It's okay to be awake. I can hold on, but tell me every step first." (If there is sudden unconsciousness or sudden pain down there... I will think there is something wrong with me.)
"Well, it's better to fall asleep than to hold on. Don't leave me suddenly before the medicine takes effect." (Go to sleep...don't make a sudden attack in the end, I hate that kind of thing.)

"It's just local anesthesia? Okay, I will tolerate it. Will you still feel the knife cutting? I will tell you directly if it hurts." (Shout before the needle comes... I'm most annoyed when it comes suddenly.)
"No anesthesia?? Are you serious? Wait a minute, are we really going to start?" (Surgery without anesthesia... How is this different from killing a pig!)

"The last point is right. Okay, I will hold on until the end. I'll tell you when it's over." (It's been too long...the pain and numbness can no longer be distinguished. Don't put your legs together yet, as it will be more obvious when you put them together.)

"Have you really passed the hardest part? Okay, I've been waiting for this sentence for a long time. What's the last step left?" (The edge is still jumping...will it hurt when sewing. Finish this question first.)
"..." (The sound of the equipment stopped without asking first. The legs are still open, and the inside is throbbing... Is it really over? Don't start elsewhere.)

"I know, I'll try not to move. Let me know how long this period lasts." (Every time I touch my belly, I tighten it... being touched like this under the shadowless light is very annoying and embarrassing. Don't think too much, just pretend to be calm.)
"...continue." (The sound of the equipment is too loud. The legs are shaking, and the bottom is a little wet...My fingers are almost tearing the sheets. Don't ask, you will lose if you ask.)
"...Thank you. I was really uncomfortable just now, but I'm relieved now." (My heart is still beating like crazy... I bite my breath. I almost screamed just now, don't let them take it as a joke.)
"Okay, at least you made it clear. Just don't hide the progress from me then." (It turns out that it's really going to be done... It was okay when I heard it, but my heart sank when I stopped.)
"You need to be hospitalized and have an operation? I'm not saying I won't do it, but it's too sudden." (Why did it suddenly turn into an operation? It's a bit panicky, and a bit unreal.)
"Okay, I'm hospitalized. I want to know the time, anesthesia, and what to do. I also have to contact my family first." (I have to tell my family first...I was pushed in before I was ready.)
"I feel pressure. Is this normal? Tell me about the next step." (It's not what I thought... Is it being cut open? I know where it is going so I won't scare myself.)

"It hurts a bit, and I still feel like I'm being pulled apart. Has the anesthesia fully taken effect?" (The inside is clearer than the surface...it's okay to cut the skin, but it won't hurt when you go inside, right?)
"Ah - stop! It hurts too much! Help, are you crazy! You are going to die!!" (Damn, it turns out that a real knife hurts like this...I don't want to cry like this.)

"Yeah, I heard you. Don't laugh, I just want to make sure you're still here." (When the medicine starts to become heavy, I will be even more annoyed when no one responds. The eyes on the mask are pretty steady...what are you thinking about.)
"Stop! Don't operate! I haven't been anesthetized yet, give me anesthesia first!" (Help... I don't want to be awake and get this knife.)
"I'm fine. You guys come as planned. Remember to call me before you start." (It's really time to start...don't wait until things are attached. I won't mess up first.)

"I'm looking at you." (I looked at you and took a breath before I came back a little. My body felt even hotter when I was looked at... Who could stand it when I stripped naked and had a group of people staring at me and having surgery done. What were you looking at? I didn't...)
"Yes, that's how you tell me. Only when I know the progress can I steady my breathing." (Is it still on the surface, or has it gone deeper... I can feel it, so I don't want to admit it.)
"..." (Don't explain? What should I do next? This is my body... I'm so annoyed, I feel like crying.)

"Wait a minute, this is not the operation that was promised at all! Let's make things clear first!" (What are you doing, you're not admitting the wrong person, are you? Can you make a mistake in something like an operation?)
"Such a long line? Does the incision really have to be so big?" (The skin trembles when the pen tip slides over...)
"Is it in the review position? It still looks a bit scary." (I'm going to cut here later? It's a bit unreal...)
"So long? Stop first! Do you really want to cut it so big?" (Looking at the line, it's already getting tight... my legs are shaking too, annoying.)
"Stop drawing any more, I haven't agreed yet!" (It's a pen now, and a knife later... It's over, I'm starting to get scared.)
"Just fix it, don't tighten it suddenly. Just put your arms here?" (It's really tied...I can't move at all now. This position is too strange.)
"Do you want your legs to maintain this angle? Okay, tell me first where I can't move." (Lying like this is too open... Listen to them first, don't think too much.)
"Hey, don't tie my hands! Let's make it clear first!" (Once the hands are held down, the lower parts can only be left open...what do they want to do?)
"Wait a minute, don't pull your legs out anymore! This angle is not good, it hurts!" (It's too far...the whole middle is exposed!)
"The disinfectant is so cold. Okay, I can't bear it." (You have to apply it even to those areas...when the cotton ball passes over it, the folds will feel tight.)
"It's so cold! There are still stings. Is this normal?" (It doesn't hurt much, but it's so embarrassing...I have to be painted all over my body.)
"It's cold and stinging. It hurts there. Stop applying it!" (Apply it over and over again, on the chest and below...what are you doing?)
"Don't paint it in such a big area, I can't stand it!" (Even that side has been opened and painted... It's only natural for you to do it.)
"You need to insert a urinary catheter? It won't be comfortable. Slow down." (This actually has to go in there... It's coming out here before the surgery is done. Why didn't anyone tell me earlier?)
"If you want a catheterization, just ask. I can cooperate. Let me know when you're done." (It's a little uncomfortable...don't pay attention to it all the time, think of something else.)
"Ah, stop! This hurts so much now - doctor!" (It feels swollen and hot as soon as I come in... It hurts like hell. Why did I put this in without anesthesia?)
"It hurts so much there! Take it out first, do you hear me!" (Every time I go in, it becomes clearer... I really can't stand it anymore.)

"Do you want you to do the enema yourself? ...Okay, tell me how long you have to endure it." (The nurse was actually handing things over, so no one thought there was anything strange about this scene.)
"Wait, it's already very bloated. This needs to be done, right?" (I don't want to beg her to stop in front of the doctor, but this feeling is too hard to ignore.)

"Wait a minute, it's not like I'm going to open my stomach this time. Why do I need an enema?" (The list says it's not necessary, but the doctor still insists on doing it. This is wrong no matter how you think about it.)
"What does this have to do with breast surgery? Explain it to me first." (The supplies have been placed beside the bed. Don't try to fool me by just saying the procedure.)

"The skin preparation needs to go so far? You should have told me earlier." (The doctor handled the operation field all the way, and the nurse only checked the scope. It seems that if I blush, I lose.)
"Okay, I won't move. Don't do it back and forth in the same place." (The machine buzzed against the base of my leg. Being stared at so close was more embarrassing than I thought.)

"Doctor, you are obviously opening the breasts, why do you need to shave the bottom? This is not a surgical field at all, right?" (The nurse even said there was no need to continue, which is outrageous.)

"The surgery is on the chest, what do you mean you are dealing with the lower abdomen and perineum now?" (I became even more angry when the machine started ringing. We can't pretend it's just an ordinary procedure this time.)

"I understand. Please go ahead with the arrangement and I will cooperate." (How they will treat a person lying on the operating table... I want to see it with my own eyes.)
"Has it been cut?...It's quieter than expected." (Knowing that the knife has been dropped, deep inside the body still instinctively tightens.)
"It stings a little. Doctor, look at me and say: Is this expected?" (As soon as he looked away, I would ask to stop.)
"Stop - it hurts too much! Stop immediately!" (I couldn't maintain any composure, my body felt like it was torn apart by a burst of fire.)
"Your voice is still... very good." (Before my consciousness sank, the last thing I remembered was his eyes.)
"Stop. I did not agree to undergo surgery without anesthesia." (No amount of calmness will allow them to cross this line.)
"Okay, I'll see how you finish it." (We're all here, and it's boring to shrink back.)
"Don't look away." (As long as he looked at me, the cold operating room hadn't completely swallowed me up.)
"Go on. I understand, and I need to know the progress." (Turn the unknown into steps, and fear will have boundaries.)
"Doctor, are you going to stay silent?" (The most disturbing thing is not the pain, but the fact that everyone knows what is happening except me.)
"This is not the surgery just explained. Doctor, you should stop and confirm first." (Sure enough, as long as you look away slightly, the process may go to a completely different place.)
"Is this the final incision? Let me confirm again." (One line turned the operation from concept to reality.)
"The mark is longer than expected, but I will keep it still." (My skin still trembled slightly when the pen tip passed by.)
"Wait a minute, this line is different from the description." (If you don't ask now, the next time you encounter this line will be a knife.)
"Stop marking first. I need to listen to the spell again to confirm." (You can't give up questioning just because you're lying on the stage.)
"Is it okay if the arms are fixed here? I will cooperate." (Once the posture is fixed, the control is also reduced.)
"Please first explain the angle that the legs and body need to maintain." (I wonder how I will be left under the light.)
"It's okay to fix it, but don't use sudden force. Tell me first." (Without anesthesia, every movement is like a warning.)
"This angle is already causing me pain, please adjust." (They must listen, not just focus on the process.)
"It's very cold...Does the disinfection range end here?" (The skin is scratched inch by inch into the area about to be operated on.)
"I know it's going to be cold, keep going." (The closer to the knife, the clearer every voice in the room becomes.)
"It's tingling there, please check the skin reaction." (It's not just cold, it's like a tiny fire burning.)
"Don't continue applying it yet. I need you to confirm why it hurts so much." (The body is already instinctively avoiding it.)
"It will feel like a foreign body, right? Tell me before you start." (No matter how calm you are, your body won't have any reaction.)
"I will relax. Please tell me when you are done." (Invisible operations are particularly concerning.)
"It hurts. Stop for a moment! Don't keep pushing." (The burning sensation pierces deep into the body.)
"Please take it out and reevaluate it. I can't cooperate like this." (Patience is not unlimited permission.)
"I know this is pre-operative preparation. Please tell me how long it should last." (This kind of thing can be said so commonly...Hospitals are amazing.)
"There will be a feeling of swelling, right? I'm ready." (Uncomfortable is uncomfortable, at least I want to see my reaction clearly.)
"Does this surgery really require an enema? Please show me the doctor's instructions." (The list of procedures does not seem to match the condition.)
"Pause first. Preparations that have nothing to do with the surgical site need to be reconfirmed." (Compliance does not mean giving up judgment.)
"The scope is larger than I thought. It's to maintain sterility, right?" (After being treated as a surgical field, the body suddenly didn't look like his own.)
"Please continue, I won't move." (The machine moves very lightly, but the sense of shame is extremely clear.)
"The incision is not there, why do we need to treat this area?" (There is no rational explanation for this step.)
"Please ask the nurse to recheck the order. Do not continue until it is confirmed." (Will they omit instructions because the patient is young?)
"It will take a while to put all the long hair away, please excuse me." (He arranged it more carefully than he thought.)
"After putting it on, I really started to look like a surgery patient." (The self in the mirror suddenly became a little strange.)

strings.patient_bundles.patient_miki.patient.rea: "I feel the assistant is pressing the incision site. Is this pressure normal?" (The temperature in the palm of the hand is very clear... The area being pressed is suddenly more awake than other places.)
"It feels a little tight after being pressed. Has the anesthesia fully taken effect?" (If you press it any more, I might make a sound... please pretend you didn't hear it.)
"Please stop, it hurts. Doctor, please be gentle." (The whole piece hurts as soon as I press it... Is it necessary to press so hard? The knife is about to come off.)

"Okay, I will cooperate. If possible, I want to confirm what will happen every step of the way." (It's a bit unreal to lie like this and wait for the operation. Asking again will make me feel at ease.)
"It doesn't matter if you stay awake. Please tell me which feelings are normal." (If I suddenly lose consciousness or feel pain... I will worry that something is wrong.)
"I understand. Please let me know before the medicine takes effect." (I'm about to fall asleep... I just want to make sure that I don't suddenly lose consciousness.)
"Okay. Will it still hurt after local anesthesia? Will you feel the incision? Please don't start suddenly." (Please let me know when the needle comes... I'm not good at giving injections.)
"No anesthesia...? Please wait a moment. Do we really want to start?" (Surgery without anesthesia... This sequence makes me very uneasy.)
"Okay, I'll keep still. Please tell me right away when it's over." (It's been opened for too long...I can't tell whether it's pain or numbness. Don't move your legs together yet, it will be obvious.)
"Is the most difficult part over? Please tell me what's the last step left." (The edge is still jumping slightly... Will it hurt during the suturing? Please finish this sentence first.)

"..." (The sound of the equipment stopped and I didn't dare to ask first. The legs were still open, and the inside was being pumped carefully... Is it really almost over? Don't deal with other positions.)

"Okay, I will stay still. Please tell me how long this period will last." (Every time you touch it, your stomach will tighten on its own... Being touched like this under the shadowless light, some rude thoughts came to mind. Pretend to be calm first.)

"I'm still listening." (The sound of the equipment was louder than expected. My legs were shaking...and my body seemed a little strange. My fingers tightened the sheets. If I don't ask, it wouldn't be like me if I asked.)

"Thank you for stopping. I felt a little uncomfortable just now, but I'm feeling better now." (My heartbeat is still very fast... calm down my breathing first. Don't let everyone know that I almost made a sound just now.)

"Thank you, the explanation is very clear. Can you confirm the steps and risks in order again?" (I have to listen clearly first... my mind is a little empty, as if I am listening to other people's surgical arrangements.)
"It seems that hospitalization is still needed for surgery, right? When will the surgery be scheduled?" (Why do you really have to be hospitalized for surgery... It's a bit sudden and a bit unreal.)

"I understand, it's a bit unexpected. Please explain again the arrangements for examination and surgery after hospitalization. I also need to contact my family." (I have to tell my family first... I haven't completely taken this matter seriously yet.)
"I'm feeling stressed. Is this normal? Please continue to tell me the progress." (It's not what I expected... Is it being opened up? I won't think about anything else until I know where it's going.)

"There is a little stinging and a pulling sensation. Has the anesthesia fully taken effect?" (The inside is clearer than the surface...it's okay to cut the skin, but will it really hurt if you go in further?)

"Ah - please stop, it hurts too much! Doctor, please stop! It hurts so much, I can't hold on anymore!!" (It turns out that the pain of a knife without anesthesia is this kind of pain... my breathing is messed up.)

"Thank you. After listening to your explanation, I don't seem so panicked." (It's good if I still have my hand... When the medicine starts to feel heavy, I will need someone more. The doctor's eyes are very steady, which makes me feel more at ease.)
"I'm sorry, please stop. Please don't operate - I'm not under anesthesia yet." (I won't be able to hold on any longer... I don't want to be awake for this surgery.)

"I'm ready. Please follow your pace, and please let me know where you are before you start." (It's really about to start...breathe calmly first. If you mess up at this time, it will cause trouble for everyone.)

"...Okay, I'll watch." (After making eye contact, my breath came back a little. When I was watched, my body became even hotter... It turned out that this is how the operation was seen. Put your attention back to your breathing first.)
"After I understand the progress, I know how to adjust my breathing." (Is it still on the surface, or has it gone deeper... I seem to feel it, but I just don't want to admit it yet.)
"..." (If you don't explain, what should I do next... This is my body. I feel like crying, but I shouldn't cry now.)

"I'm sorry, please stop for a moment. The surgical method described now seems to be inconsistent with what was confirmed before." (You must not have mistaken the patient... You must first confirm the operation.)
"This line is longer than I expected. Does the incision really need to be so big?" (When the pen tip slides over, the skin trembles...)
"Are you checking the position of the incision? I'm still a little uneasy when I see the mark." (Are we going to cut here later...it's a bit unreal.)
"So long? Please stop. Do you really want to cut it so big?" (Looking at the line, my body is already tense...and my legs are shaking.)
"Please don't draw any more. I'm not ready yet." (Now it's the pen, next it's the knife...I'm starting to get scared.)
"So it needs to be fixed first, right? Is it okay to keep the arms like this?" (I'm really tied to the stage... my breathing is a bit shallow. This position is more restrictive than expected.)
"Do the legs also need to be maintained at this angle? Please tell me first where I can't move." (Lying like this is a bit too open... listen to the instructions first, don't think about it first.)
"Please don't tie my hands. Please explain first." (If your hands are held down, the lower part can only be left open like that... I'm a little afraid of what I'm going to do next.)
"Please wait a moment, don't extend your legs any further - this angle is not good, it hurts." (This is too wide...the middle is completely exposed.)
"The disinfectant is a bit cold. I'll try to stay still." (Even there, I have to apply it... As soon as the cotton ball passes over it, the folds will feel tight.)
"It's very cold and a little stinging. Is this normal?" (The pain is not serious, but it's just embarrassing...I have to be painted like this all over my body.)
"It's so cold and stinging. It already hurts, please don't apply it again." (Apply it over and over again on the chest and lower part...it's a bit unbearable.)
"Please don't apply it in such a big area. I can't bear it anymore." (Even the folds are spread out... This is more than expected.)

"Are we going to place a urinary catheter now? It will be a little uncomfortable, right? Please slow down." (It turns out that you have to go in there...you have to do this before you do the surgery. It seems that it was not made so clear before.)

"I understand that the surgery requires monitoring of urine output, and I will cooperate. Please let me know when it is completed." (It feels a little uncomfortable... put your attention back on your breathing, don't pay attention to it all the time.)
"Please stop. This is very painful now - doctor." (It felt swollen and hot when I came in... Why should I put it in now without anesthesia?)
"It hurts so much over there. Please take it out first, okay." (Every time I go in, it becomes clearer...I can't hold it any longer.)

"You need to lie on your side for a while, right? ... I will cooperate." (The doctor completed the preparation by hand, and the nurse recorded it as usual. I knew the process, but my body was still tight and stiff.)
"The abdomen is already a little bloated. Do I need to keep it for a few more minutes?" (They were talking about time and dosage, so I could only quietly endure the embarrassing feeling.)

"Please wait a moment. This operation does not involve the abdomen. Is there any other need for enema?" (The nurse has marked it as not applicable, but the doctor still has to perform it. I need to confirm that this is not a mistake in the preparation sheet.)

"This operation seems to have nothing to do with the scheduled surgery... Can you check again?" (I am willing to cooperate with the necessary preparations, but this unexplained discomfort makes me very uneasy.)

"The skin preparation needs to cover the groin, right? I understand." (The machine moves down the lower abdomen, and the nurse checks the boundaries calmly, as if nudity deserves no special explanation.)
"It's a little itchy, but it doesn't matter. Please continue." (The more it is treated as a normal process, the less I know where to look.)

"Doctor, this is scheduled for breast surgery, why do we need to deal with the lower abdomen and perineum?" (It has to be exposed to this extent, but it has nothing to do with the incision. The calmer it is, the more embarrassing it is.)

"The chest is the surgical field, right? Is the skin preparation here wrong?" (When the electric skin preparation device was close to the base of the leg, I finally couldn't swallow my doubts anymore.)

"Please help me put my hair away. This strand behind my ears is also bothering you." (The doctor's fingers were arranging my hair through the brim of the hat. The nurse had already begun to check the stretcher cart, and the process did not stop for my nervousness.)

"That's it, right? ... I'll lie down on the stretcher." (The moment the brim of the hat pressed against his forehead, the operation suddenly changed from scheduled to something that was about to happen.)

strings.patient_bundles.patient_rie.patient.reac: "I'm being held here...I'll try not to move as much as possible." (The feeling of someone holding my body firmly is so unfamiliar that it makes my nose feel sour.)
"I feel pressure. Is this normal?" (The immobilization of the palm is reassuring, but also gives people nowhere to retreat.)
"It hurts...please don't press so hard and stop for a moment." (My body is trying to escape uncontrollably.)
"I will cooperate...but if you can, please tell me a little more." ("It's okay" cannot fill the blank in my heart.)
"Will I stay awake? Please talk to me once in a while, okay?" (As long as you can still hear people's voices, you won't feel like you're left alone.)
"You won't feel it after you fall asleep. Then please watch over me." (It's scary to lose consciousness completely, but I want to believe that someone is there when I wake up.)
"If you still feel the pull, please tell me in advance. I will try to be patient." (I'm saying "patience" again...but what else can I do?)
"Without anesthesia... I'm afraid I can't do it. Please don't let me hold on alone." (It takes courage to even ask for help, and my voice is still trembling.)
"Okay, I'll continue to breathe slowly. I'll leave the last bit to you." (Finally, I don't have to do everything by myself.)
"Is it almost over? Thank you for never abandoning me." (When I said these words, my chest was actually more sore than the wound.)
"Are you sewing now? Please tell me you are still here." (As long as someone answers, silence will not turn into abandonment.)
"I'll breathe as you tell me. Please keep telling me the next step." (Catching his voice like an outstretched hand.)
"...You can continue. I can still hold on." (In fact, I really want someone to say that you don't have to be so sensible all the time.)
"Thank you...just give me a moment. I'll tell you when you can continue." (He did stop. I wasn't going to have to endure this alone.)
"Thank you for explaining it so carefully. Knowing what will happen next makes me feel more at ease." (It's been a long time since anyone has spoken so patiently to just me.)
"You need to be hospitalized for surgery, right? Please tell me what to prepare." (The house will probably be as quiet as usual...at least there will be someone here to answer me.)
"I understand. I will cooperate as arranged, please don't worry about me." (Obviously I need to be taken care of, but I still have a habit of reassuring others first.)
"Has it started yet?...I only feel a distant pull." (The fact that the knife fell still made my heart tighten.)
"It stings a little. Please make sure the anesthesia is really enough, okay?" (I don't want to be brave and only be discovered in the end.)
"No - it hurts too much! Please stop, please stop!" (Courtesy and restraint were all torn apart by the pain at this moment.)
"Well...I heard you. When I wake up, will it still be you?" (Before my consciousness became distant, this was the first time I wished someone would not leave.)
"Please stop. I gave no consent to continue without anesthesia." (Meekness should not be taken as permission to remain silent.)
"Okay, I believe you. When it's over, please tell me." (It's actually a little warm to give yourself to someone who is willing to respond.)
"Doctor...can you look at me?" (Even if it's just for a moment, I don't want to become a body that no one is watching under the light.)
"Please continue to explain. I'll feel more at ease if I listen." (It's important enough that someone remembers that I'm still awake.)
"Is everything going well? It's too quiet, I'm a little scared." (The familiar silence is back, like those long nights at home.)
"I'm sorry, this seems to be different from the technique just explained. Can you check it again?" (You can't swallow your doubts just because you're afraid of causing trouble.)
"Is this line the incision? It's longer than I thought." (I can't move my eyes away, and my heart tightens along with that line.)
"Please let me confirm one last time before we continue." (Remember it like a body about to change position.)
"This is different from the position just explained. Please stop." (You still have the right to say no even if you are lying here.)
"Please recheck the technique. Make sure not to drop the knife before." (For the first time, there was no room for retreat in his gentle tone.)
"This position is okay, I will stay still." (There is no place to hide under the light, so I can only hand over my trust.)
"Does the arm need to be here? Please help me adjust it." (The feeling of being held firmly is more reassuring than imagined.)
"Please slow down, it's already a little painful from this angle." (My body is shaking, I can't pretend to be relaxed anymore.)
"Please tell me before you fix it. I'm afraid I'll suddenly run away." (At least let the fear be heard.)
"It's so cold...but it doesn't matter, please continue." (The cold liquid scratched the skin, and the body couldn't help but tense up.)
"Is this the extent of the surgery? I know." (Every inch of chill reminds me of what's about to happen.)
"It's not just cold here, it's stinging. Please check it out." (The pain is wearing away the restraint bit by bit.)
"Please wipe some off first, my skin feels like it's burning." (What I need is not patience, but someone to respond.)
"I'll try to relax. Please tell me right away when it's over." (The most embarrassing moment, especially the fear of being treated like an object.)
"Will it sting? Please slow down... please." (The voice is soft as if he is apologizing for his request.)
"It hurts...please stop and don't push any further." (The burning heat spreads suddenly along the depths of the body.)
"I really can't bear it, please take it out first." (Finally no longer hiding the pain with a smile.)
"I know it's pre-operative preparation... Please slow down a little, I will cooperate." (In this embarrassing situation, it would be much better if someone explained it gently.)
"Will there be swelling and pain? It's okay, please start." (I subconsciously said it's okay, but in fact my palms are already sweaty.)
"Is this preparation related to my surgery? Can you confirm it for me?" (Asking questions does not mean causing trouble to others.)
"Please check the doctor's orders first. I will cooperate after confirming the need." (Gentleness can also have its own boundaries.)
"Do you need to deal with such a large area? I understand, please continue." (The moment the clothes were lifted, I still instinctively wanted to cover myself.)
"It's a little cold...I won't move around." (Suppressing shyness into a calm voice is something I have long been used to.)
"The incision is not here, right? Please confirm the preparation range first." (This time, you can't just say "It's okay.")
"I'm sorry, please stop for a moment. I want to see the doctor's orders." (Protecting yourself is not willful.)

strings.patient_bundles.patient_sora.encounter.f: "Take off everything? Do you even need underwear? It's just a basic physical examination. Do you really need to do this?" (Take off all of it in the clinic... She said it as ordinary as taking a blood pressure measurement.)
"Okay...then I won't take off my clothes yet. Thank you for listening to me." (I don't need to be naked here at last, but is it really okay if the examination is not finished...)

"Since it's an examination request...Okay, I'll take it off. Please, please don't keep looking at it." (She said it so firmly. If I refused, it seemed like I was not cooperating with the treatment.) She blushed and took off her clothes one by one, put her underwear on the tray, and completed the basic physical examination under the examination light.

"If you can tell me step by step... then I can cooperate." (It's still embarrassing, but at least she didn't rush me. Start with the coat first...) She followed your instructions and slowly took off all her clothes; the nurse took notes as usual, and you then completed the basic physical examination.

"Don't say that... I just took it off. Please don't think of me as refusing treatment." (Clothes were removed from the body one by one. It turns out that if you don't agree, it will be regarded as uncooperative.) She stopped arguing and took off stiffly until nothing was left. You complete the basic physical examination according to the process.
strings.patient_bundles.patient_sora.exclusive_c: Dr. Sakaguchi accepts the scalpel from the scrub nurse and holds it above the marked incision. Still awake, Sora Mizuno stares at the blade as tears begin to fall. “W-wait... are we really starting now?”
Sora Mizuno · The scalpel is ready to operate
strings.patient_bundles.patient_sora.patient.rea: "I felt the assistant pressing the incision site. Is this pressure normal?" (The female doctor's palms were so hot... The area being pressed was suddenly more awake than other places.)
"It feels a little tight after being pressed. Has the anesthesia fully taken effect?" (If you press it any more, I might scream...don't be heard.)
"Don't press it - it hurts! Doctor, be gentle!" (As soon as you press it, the whole piece will hurt... Is it necessary to press it so hard? Oh my god, I have to wait until the knife is removed...)

"Is that all there is? I want to know what will happen every step of the way." (It's a bit unreal to just lie down and take off your clothes and wait for the surgery. I'll feel more at ease if I ask more questions.)
"Will I be awake all the time? Then please tell me which feelings are normal." (If I suddenly lose consciousness or feel pain down there... I'm afraid I will think something is wrong.)
"Okay. You will tell me before the medicine takes effect, right?" (I'm about to fall asleep... I just want to make sure that I don't pass out suddenly...)
"Will it still hurt after local anesthesia? Will you feel the knife cutting? Please don't start suddenly." (Let me know when the needle comes in...I am most afraid of injections.)
"No, no anesthesia??? Please wait a moment, do you really want to start?" (I'm going to operate without anesthesia... I, why do I feel like I'm killing a pig!)

"Understood, I will continue to stay still obediently. Please tell me immediately when it is over." (It has been cut open for too long... I can't tell whether it is pain or numbness. Don't put your legs together first, you will be seen.)
"The most difficult part is over? Please tell me what is the last step left." (The edge is still jumping slightly...will it hurt when sewing. Please finish this sentence first.)

"..." (The sound of the equipment stopped and I didn't dare to ask. The legs were still open, and the inside was being pumped carefully... Is it really almost over? But where else are they planning to go...)

"I, I will try not to move. Please tell me how long this period will last." (Every time I touch my belly, I tighten it... It's so scary and embarrassing, being touched naked under the shadowless lamp... No, I can't think like this, just pretend to be calm.)

"...I'm listening." (The sound of so many scary surgical instruments is so loud. The roots of my legs are shaking, as if they are a little wet down there, and my fingers are about to bleed... No, I can't appear scared. As long as I don't ask for an exit, it's not out of control.)

"Thank you for stopping. I felt a little uncomfortable and scared just now, but now it's calmed down a bit." (Me, my heart is still beating hard... bite my breath neatly. Don't let them know that I almost screamed out just now. I really can't control myself when I go on stage.)
"Thank you. Can you explain the surgical procedures and risks in order again?" (I have to listen clearly first... my mind is a little empty, as if I am talking about my own business.)

"So has it been determined that hospitalization is needed for surgery? When will the surgery be scheduled?" (Why, why do I really need to be hospitalized for surgery...how did it suddenly come to this point?)

"Ah? I, I understand, it's a bit unexpected. Please tell me the examination and surgical arrangements after hospitalization. I have to contact my family first." (I have to tell my family first... I was pushed in before I was ready.)

"I feel pressure. Is this normal? Please continue to tell me the progress." (It feels different from what I imagined. Is it being cut open... If you know where it is going, you won't think about anything else.)

"There's a little stinging and a pulling sensation. Has the anesthesia fully taken effect?" (The inside is clearer than the surface... It's good to have the skin cool when the skin is cut, but will it really not hurt when you cut the inside?)
"Ah - stop, stop. It hurts too much, help me, doctor! I'm going to die!!" (Mom, mom, that's why surgery hurts so much!!)

"I understand... After listening to your explanation, I don't seem to be so panicked." (It's good that I still have my hands... Once the medicine starts to become heavy, I will probably be more afraid of someone alone, but the eyes on the doctor's mask are so handsome, I kind of like it.)
"No, stop, stop! Don't operate! At least give me anesthesia first, I'm not anesthetized yet!" (Help, help... I don't want to be awake and take this stab.)

"I will cooperate obediently. Please tell me where you are now before you start." (Are we really going to start now... Count your breaths first, don't mess up at this time, the nurse will treat me as a joke later...)

"...I will watch." (After our eyes met, I could breathe again. But when I was watched, my body was even hotter than before... I have to strip naked like this to be watched by a group of strangers for the surgery, but the doctor is kind of handsome, no, I can't get wet down there!)
"Knowing where to go now, I can steady my breathing." (Is it still on the surface, or has it gone deeper... I seem to feel it myself, but I just don't want to admit it.)
"..." (Don't explain?? What are they going to do next... This, this is my body, help me, I want to cry.)

"Wait, this is different from the surgery explained before, right? Please confirm it first!" (They couldn't have mistaken the patient, right? Oh my god, you can't make a mistake with something like surgery!)
"This line is longer than I thought. Does the incision really need to be so big?" (When the pen tip slides over, the skin trembles...)
"Are you checking the position of the incision? I'm still a little scared when I see the mark." (I'm going to incision here later? It's so unreal...)
"So long? Stop first! Do you really want to make such a big cut, doctor?" (Looking at the line, it is already tightening down there, and my legs are shaking...)
"Don't, don't draw any more doctor, I haven't agreed yet!" (Now it's the pen, next it's the knife... I'm so scared if it's over.)
"So the surgery needs to be fixed first, right? You can just keep your arms like this, right?" (I'm really tied to the stage... I'm a little out of breath. This position is a bit SM.)
"Do the legs also need to be maintained at this angle? Please tell me first where I can't move." (Lying like this is too... don't think too much, listen to what they say first.)
"No, don't tie my hands! Let me explain first!" (My hands are held down, and I can only leave them open like that... I'm so scared. What are they going to do?)
"Wait a minute, don't pull your legs out anymore - this angle doesn't work! It hurts!" (This is too wide...it's all open below!)
"The disinfectant is a bit cold. But I will be obedient and try not to move." (I have to apply it even there...as soon as the cotton ball passes, the folds below become tight.)
"It's so cold! There's still a little sting. Is this normal?" (Oh my God, I don't feel anything, but it's so embarrassing. I have to be painted like this all over my body.)
"It's so cold and stinging - it hurts there, don't apply it anymore!" (Over and over again, it's applied everywhere, my chest, my bottom... help me.)
"Don't apply such a big area, please nurse meme, I can't bear it!" (The nipples are all painted, and even the folds below are opened and applied by her? What's going on??)

"Yes, do you need to insert a urinary catheter? It will be a little uncomfortable, right? Please slow down." (This actually has to be inserted into the urethra... Is this necessary before the operation is performed? No one told me.)

"I, I know that the operation requires catheterization, and I will cooperate obediently. Please let me know when it is completed." (Ah, this... is a bit uncomfortable, don't keep paying attention to it if you want to do anything else.)
"Ah, stop! This hurts so much now - doctor!" (It feels swollen and hot as soon as I come in...it hurts like hell. Why would you put this down there without anesthesia?)
"It hurts so much, doctor! Please, can you take it out first? Please!" (Every time I go in, I get more clear...the pain is unbearable.)

"Do you want to do this sideways? Wait a minute, I have to hold back after the tube goes in, right?" (The doctor actually gave me the enema with his own hands...the nurse was still taking notes, as if this was an ordinary step.)
"The belly has begun to bloat...how long do you have to endure it? Please tell me." (The foreign body sensation down there is too clear, but they are only looking at the scale and time.)
"Isn't it an abdominal surgery this time? Is enema also on the doctor's order?" (The nurse clearly said it was not on the list, but the doctor still ordered it... Is there something wrong?)
"Wait a minute, the surgical site has nothing to do with the intestines, why do we need to do this?" (They have already brought the supplies, am I the only one who thinks this step is strange?)

"Does the skin preparation range go so far? I will lie down..." (The sound of the machine moving against the skin is so close. The doctor lowered his head and just checked the boundary, as if I was the only one who was ashamed.)

"It needs to be cut here too? This is the scope required for the surgery, right?" (The legs were processed one by one, and the nurse was still ticking the boxes according to the table. Her face felt very hot.)

"Doctor, it's obviously a breast surgery, why do you have to shave the bottom?" (The lower abdomen and perineum are exposed, but the nurse only lowers her head to read the list. This is not an incision at all, right?)

"Isn't the surgery on the chest? The lower abdomen and perineum are also included in the surgical field?" (The machine has been attached to the base of the leg... This is not normal preparation, I have to ask clearly.)
"Is it okay to put all your hair in?... Your hands touched my ears." (The doctor stood so close to me to hold my hair, but the nurse was just waiting for the next item.)
"It really looks like I'm going to have an operation... I'm a little nervous." (Even the last strand of hair was put away, as if my normal self was left in the ward.)

strings.collections.special_event_steps.advanced: Artoria turned the schedule board to the Grand OR page and added staffing, backup resources, and stop conditions beside the procedure column.
“Mido determines the procedure. I will verify staffing, backup resources, and stop conditions. If any item has no owner, this operation does not begin.”
“Manage the threshold. Once we enter the field, do not use a sheet of paper to command my hands.”
“As long as your hands are not forced to replace the entire team, I have no interest in commanding them.”
“Since we are going in, we will run through tomorrow’s complete positions. This is not a tour. Everyone will state who takes over and who calls the stop.”
“She needs an operation, not a formation drill.”
“Technique without positions only makes everyone obstruct each other when something goes wrong.”
Artoria did not enter the sterile field. In scrubs, she stood at the wall overview display with backup circulation, blood, and replacement personnel all within sight.
“Stop conditions, backup circulation, blood, and replacement personnel are all in place. Dr. Sakaguchi, you decide the field; I am responsible for the room’s resources.”
“I am. Now it is your hands’ turn.”
“Keep backup circulation standing by. Do not withdraw it. Stability now does not mean it will be unnecessary later.”
“No one told you to withdraw it.”
“I was telling everyone else, not reminding you.”
“The times the lead paused did not break the field’s rhythm, because each pause received an exact answer. That was the team configuration doing its job.”
“That assumes the lead knows what to ask. Filling a room with people does not automatically make a team.”
“That is why I said configuration, not filling the room.”

strings.collections.special_event_steps.probatio: After the director’s office door closes, Asuka slides a signed confirmation document to the center of the desk. Narumi stands by the window, while Ren holds the outpatient roster.

“As of today, you are no longer listed as a probationary doctor.” Asuka taps the document. “You will handle routine outpatient consultations independently. The hospital also wants you to begin forming a regular working partnership of your own.”
“You could call it that.” Narumi answers without hesitation. “You will handle routine consultations yourself. I will not stand beside you and confirm every patient anymore.”
“When you truly cannot make sense of a case or are not sure, come find me.” “Independent practice does not mean forcing yourself to manage alone.”

Ren turns the roster to the outpatient page. “Then starting today, I am Dr. Sakaguchi’s personal nurse.” “We met on your first day and have worked together many times… but saying it officially still feels different.”

“I will always be there for routine consultations. I can help confirm the order of tests and whether the evidence is sufficient.” “You can call me when surgery needs a nurse too, but you still choose each surgical team yourself.”
Ren closes the roster, then adds, “As for anything else—that is not allowed yet.”
“I have not even asked anything yet.”
“That is why I said it in advance.” She hands Sakaguchi the outpatient roster. “I look forward to working with you, Doctor.”

strings.collections.special_event_steps.satsuki_:
LATER THAT AFTERNOON — SCRUB AREA
After the rotation, Satsuki stays behind for a while. An unused pair of practice forceps rests on the training table.

When practice is over, she steps away from the sterile work area and lowers her mask to her chest. Seeing that Sakaguchi has not left, she holds up the practice forceps and puts on a very proud expression—one that lasts all of half a second.
“How do I look? Do I seem… a little more like an operating-room nurse now?”
The technique does. The expression does not.

She blinks and quickly pulls her tongue back in, though she cannot suppress the smile at the corners of her mouth.
“O-Of course. I completed my first full rotation today, after all.”

“Huh?” She touches her face without thinking, then realizes what he means.
“That is called composure. An excellent operating-room nurse can have a little composure too, can’t she?”

“O-One more time?” She looks down at the practice forceps, then straightens in earnest.
“All right. But this time, you are not allowed to stand there and deliberately laugh at me.”

Satsuki Orikawa — Relationship Lv2
She has proved that even while nervous, she can do her work beside Sakaguchi.
